clue.text: Better gift son lost to trickery Esau's position, not Jacob's

indicators.note: the letters are tricked out of their order, as Esau's birthright was tricked away, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jacob's cunning cost his brother Esau the better gift and the status of the elder son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost to trickery' signals an anagram of BETTER GIFT SON. In Genesis Esau was born first, but Jacob tricked him out of his birthright and blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau was born before his twin Jacob, so his rank was that of the eldest child, the one born ahead of any sibling.

clue.text: Remarkably cheap beer used to make woman swell out

definitions.text: used to make woman swell out

parts.note: a farthing was the smallest old British coin, a quarter of a penny, so anything costing one was remarkably cheap
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Drinking cheap beer, the clue jokes, will give a woman a swollen figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A FARTHING was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny, a byword for a trifling sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooped petticoat of Tudor times, worn under a skirt to spread it out widely from the hips.

clue.text: What needs some decorum ballroom dance

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words decorum ballroom are taken, a run spanning both

explanation.surface: Asks what a ballroom dance requires: a measure of decorum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals a run of letters hidden across decoRUM BAllroom. 'ballroom' looks like part of the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban dance in a lively rhythm, also performed in competitive ballroom dancing.

clue.text: Essential items needed by the board

definitions.text: Essential items needed by the board

parts.words: Essential items needed by the board
parts.note: read as the vital goods a company's directors require, but the board is a dining table and the items are the plates and cutlery laid on it

explanation.surface: A company's directors list the necessities they cannot run without.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates, cutlery and glasses are the goods set on a dining table, which an old word calls the board.

clue.text: Almost identical rocks piled up in a circle

indicators.note: almost the whole word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: identical means equal
a tor is a hill topped with a pile of rocks, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Identical stones stacked into a ring, like a prehistoric monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter from EQUAL, giving EQUA. A TOR is a rocky hilltop typical of the moors of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The great circle of latitude dividing Earth's northern and southern hemispheres.

clue.text: Pianist performing at either end of grand social occasion

indicators.note: the word for performing is split so that it sits at both ends of the other pieces

parts.note: an act on stage is on
a do is a party or social occasion

explanation.surface: A pianist plays at the start and finish of a grand society event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at either end of' splits the performing word in two around the others. John Ogdon was a British concert pianist, joint winner of the 1962 Tchaikovsky Competition.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ogdon was a celebrated English concert pianist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: What you want in kitchen? Bread's the thing to start with

parts.note: bread is slang for money, as is tin
an opener is the first item on a programme, the thing to start with

explanation.surface: A cook is told bread is the first thing needed in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread looks like food, but here it is slang for money, as is TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget for cutting into cans is a standard piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Catch outlaw up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban

explanation.surface: An order to catch a fugitive bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab or arrest someone, informally.

clue.text: Mass of pulses

definitions.meaning: a metric unit of mass, a thousandth of a kilogram
a name for chickpeas and other edible pulses grown in Asia

explanation.definitionFit: A unit of weight in the metric system, and also the word for chickpeas and related legumes.

clue.text: Sad man of the upper classes to be inspiration for waltz

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
Dan is a man's name
U is an old label for upper-class usage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A melancholy aristocrat becomes a composer's muse for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' distinctions of British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss II named his most famous waltz after the river, which inspired it.

clue.text: Most economical copy packed in box

indicators.note: one piece is packed inside the box word

parts.note: a chest is a box
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: A duplicate stuffed into a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a word meaning low in price, so the least costly option.

clue.text: Relation is extremely nice — sigh of relief

indicators.note: only the extremes of the word nice are taken, its first and last letters

parts.note: phew is an exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: A relative is lovely, to everyone's relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of nice, N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family relation.

clue.text: Unrestrained anger with tax (VAT) changing

indicators.note: the letters of the three words change their order

explanation.surface: Fury at a tax, VAT, being altered is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges ANGER, TAX and VAT. VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive, going beyond reasonable limits, without restraint.

clue.text: A foreign rascal exposed but none the worse off

parts.note: un is French for a
an imp is a mischievous rascal
aired means brought into the open, exposed

explanation.surface: A rogue from abroad is unmasked yet suffers no harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Undamaged and as good as before, not weakened in any way.

clue.text: Provisional instruction to couturier

definitions.meaning: temporary, serving for the time being
an order to a dressmaker to sew a shift, a simple dress

explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap arrangement, and read as two words a command to sew a straight dress.

clue.text: To demolish, pound and smite violently

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about violently into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Instructions to tear down: hammer and strike hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something apart piece by piece, pulling down a structure.

clue.text: Communication in anything but English

parts.note: anything but means not

explanation.surface: A message written in any language except English.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written message, as left on a desk.

clue.text: He might take 25 to be a fool

definitions.text: He might take 25 to be a fool

parts.words: He might take 25 to be a fool
parts.note: entry 25 is the animal; a male of that animal takes it on to form a compound meaning an idiot

explanation.surface: A man accepts a donkey's role and is made to look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25-down, ASS. Put this word before it and you get a word for a fool; it is also the name for a male donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The male donkey is so called, and joined to the animal's name it makes a word for an idiot.

clue.text: Like some events neat squire turns out for?

indicators.note: the letters turn out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A smart country gentleman dresses for the horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges NEAT and SQUIRE; it also suggests dressing smartly for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-riding competitions such as show jumping and dressage are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Eternal ruin when one has yen for nothing

indicators.note: one letter goes in for another, the yen replacing the nothing

parts.note: someone's undoing is their ruin

explanation.surface: Endless ruin awaits anyone who longs for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In UNDOING (ruin), Y (yen, the Japanese currency) replaces O (nothing, zero).
explanation.definitionFit: Never dying, lasting for ever, hence everlasting.

clue.text: Rubbish discharged in a mass behind planes

indicators.note: the later pieces come behind the aircraft

parts.note: jets are planes

explanation.surface: Waste dumped en masse from the back of aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods thrown overboard from a ship to lighten it, which then wash ashore as debris.

clue.text: Girl partly frozen must drink a port

indicators.note: the girl takes another piece inside her, as one drinks

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of La Boheme, whose tiny hand is frozen in Rodolfo's aria

explanation.surface: A half-frozen girl needs a warming drink of port.
explanation.walkthrough: In Puccini's opera La Boheme, Rodolfo sings 'Che gelida manina' (Your tiny hand is frozen) to Mimi, so she is 'partly frozen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Florida with a major seaport, one of the busiest cruise harbours.

clue.text: Spent with passion, seeing so exciting a race?

parts.note: spent means exhausted, dead
heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: Lovers exhausted after passion, describing it as a thrilling contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in which competitors finish level, which makes for an exciting finish.

clue.text: Dye? The first bit on hair has upset woman

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word hair is taken
in a down entry, upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman is upset when her first attempt at dyeing her hair goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the woman's name over, as the down entry is read upwards; 'The first bit on hair' supplies the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown plant dye used to colour hair and skin.

clue.text: Important city street accommodating one business person?

indicators.note: the city and street pieces take another piece in, housing it

parts.note: the capital is a country's most important city
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A leading city's main street houses a single businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' houses the one inside, between the city and the street; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who invests money in business for profit is an example of this type, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Animal carrying burden pauses regularly

indicators.note: letters are taken at regular intervals from pauses, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A pack animal stops every so often under its load.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey, traditionally used as a beast of burden.

clue.text: Tidy kitchen finally, then have meal

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word kitchen is taken

parts.note: to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Clean up the kitchen, then sit down to dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means orderly and in good arrangement.

clue.text: Like a large dining table perhaps worker offers resident

parts.words: Like a large dining table perhaps
parts.note: a big table might be seating ten people
a worker ant is a classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A big dining table, a worker says, suits the occupant.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first phrase as SITTING TEN: a large table might seat ten diners. A sitting tenant is one already occupying a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger already living in a rented property when it is sold, with legal rights to stay.
